newsitem.title: USA: Oregon representative cooley charged with lying to voters.
newsitem.headline: Oregon representative cooley charged with lying to voters.

text.p: Rep. Wes Cooley, who withdrew from a re-election campaign after questions were raised about his honesty, has been indicted on charges he lied to Oregon voters.

According to the indictment handed up by a special grand jury meeting in the state capital of Salem, Cooley was charged with lying about his Korean War record in statements published in official voters pamphlets.
The two-count indictment was sealed pending Cooley's arraignment Friday, but a copy was obtained by Reuters.
In the 1994 voter-education pamphlets Cooley, 64, stated he served in "Army Special Forces, Korea."

But official Army records show Cooley was in basic training when the war ended, and the rancher has never been able to provide any evidence he served in the special forces, also known as the Green Berets.
Under Oregon law knowingly making a false statement to voters is a felony punishable by up to five years in prison and a $100,000 fine.

Cooley was unopposed in the Republican primary and was nominated to serve a second term representing eastern Oregon's 2nd Congressional District, but he withdrew under heavy pressure from state party leaders over the allegations.
Republican Rep. Bob Smith was nominated to replace Cooley on the ballot and easily won election last month.

A separate federal grand jury is investigating whether Cooley's wife improperly collected military widow's benefits while the two were living together and presenting themselves as a married couple, the Oregonian newspaper reported in Portland.
Cooley, who runs a ranch and nutritional supplement company near Bend, was not immediately available for comment.
